title: Fabrication of Decellularized Cartilage-derived Matrix Scaffolds
protocol: Prepare 1 L of cartilage washing solution with sterile PBS supplemented with penicillin, streptomycin, and Amphotericin B.
Wear gloves and a lab coat during harvesting.
Obtain an intact (cadaveric) joint for cartilage isolation.
Remove the skin around the joint area using a scalpel and surgical tweezer.
Remove excessive fat and muscle tissue without damaging the underlying joint.
Define the location where the joint articulates by performing extension and flexion of the joint.
Carefully remove layers of fat with a scalpel and surgical tweezer.
Remove more muscle layers with a scalpel and surgical tweezer.
Open up the joint area by removing tendons with a scalpel and surgical tweezer.
Make an incision to reach the joint cavity.
Inspect the cartilage for any macroscopic damage.
Discard the cartilage if it does not have a glossy, smooth appearance or shows evident blistering, clefts, or defects.
Use a sterile scalpel to remove the cartilage from the subchondral bone.
Cut all the way down to the subchondral bone to also remove the deep zone of the cartilage.
Drip cartilage washing solution on the cartilage regularly to prevent it from drying out.
Collect cartilage slices in 50 mL tubes containing previously prepared cartilage washing solution.
Snap freeze the cartilage slices in liquid nitrogen for 5 min.
Transfer cartilage slices into 50 mL tubes.
Lyophilize the cartilage slices for 24 hours in a freeze dryer set to approximately 0.090 mbar while maintaining an ice condenser at -51 °C.
Submerge lyophilized cartilage slices in liquid nitrogen.
Grind samples either manually or using a milling machine.
If grinding manually, use a mortar and pestle and grind the slices for approximately 45 minutes until pulverized.
If grinding with a milling machine, cool the grinding compartment with liquid nitrogen before processing.
Run the milling machine at pre-set speed for a few seconds to one minute to pulverize the cartilage slices.
Ensure all particles are ground thoroughly in the bottom of the grinding compartment when using a milling machine.
Sieve the cartilage particles using a sieve with a 0.71 mm mesh size.
Store the sieved particles in a dry place at room temperature.
Prepare the digestion solution consisting of 0.25% trypsin with EDTA supplemented with 100 U/mL penicillin, 100 μg/mL streptomycin, and 1% (v/v) Amphotericin B.
Store the digestion solution at 4 °C.
Fill each 50 mL tube with pulverized cartilage particles up to a volume of approximately 7.5 mL.
Incubate the tubes containing cartilage particles with the prepared digestion solution at 37 °C for 4 h on a roller.
Resuspend the particles by vortexing or pipetting after incubation.
Centrifuge the tubes for 20 min at 3113 x g to cause sedimentation of the cartilage particles.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat steps involving digestion and centrifugation until particles have been exposed to the digestion solution for a total of 6 cycles, each lasting 4 h.
Remove the supernatant after the final cycle by centrifuging.
Wash the particles twice in 30 mL of cartilage washing solution.
Centrifuge the particles for 20 min at 3113 x g between each wash.
Prepare a 10 mM Tris-HCl solution at pH 7.5 in deionized water.
Add 50 U/mL deoxyribonuclease and 1 U/mL ribonuclease A to the Tris-HCl buffer to obtain the nuclease solution.
Centrifuge the cartilage particles for 20 min at 3,113 x g.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged cartilage particles.
Add 30 mL of the nuclease solution to the cartilage particles and stir thoroughly.
Incubate the samples on a roller for 4 h at 37 °C.
Centrifuge the cartilage particles for 20 min at 3,113 x g after incubation.
Discard the supernatant from the centrifuged samples.
Wash the samples by adding 30 mL of 10 mM Tris-HCl solution without deoxyribonuclease and ribonuclease A to the cartilage particles.
Resuspend the particles and leave on a roller for 20 h at room temperature.
Make the detergent solution by dissolving 1% (v/v) octoxynol-1 in PBS.
Centrifuge the Tris-HCl solution from the cartilage particles for 20 min at 3,113 x g and discard the supernatant.
Add 30 mL of the prepared 1% detergent solution to the cartilage particles.
Resuspend the cartilage particles gently to avoid foaming.
Incubate the samples on a roller for 24 hours at room temperature.
Centrifuge the samples for 20 minutes at 3,113 x g to remove the detergent solution.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash the cartilage particles in 6 cycles of 8 hours each with cartilage washing solution.
Perform washing on a roller at room temperature.
Centrifuge the suspension for 20 minutes at 3,113 x g and discard the supernatant after each wash cycle.
Add fresh cartilage washing solution for subsequent wash cycles.
Store the last wash in the tubes along with the decellularized cartilage particles at -80°C.
Thaw closed tubes containing cartilage particles in warm water if they have been stored at -80°C.
Transfer the thawed cartilage particles to a cylindrical mold using a small ladle.
Press out all air-bubbles when placing the cartilage particles into the mold to avoid cavities in the scaffold.
Fill the mold until it reaches the edge with the cartilage particles.
Freeze the molds containing the cartilage particles for 10 minutes at -20°C.
Lyophilize the cartilage scaffolds within their molds for 24 hours in a freeze dryer.
Cross-link scaffolds with ultraviolet light at 30 cm distance and 365 nm overnight after lyophilization.
Sterilize the scaffolds using ethylene oxide gas.
Cut the scaffolds into thin slices of approximately 3 mm with a scalpel.
Embed the scaffold slices in a drop of 4% (w/v) alginate.
Induce cross-linking by adding an equal volume of 3.7% non-buffered formalin containing 20 mM CaCl₂ to the alginate embedding solution.
Dehydrate the samples by placing them in a graded ethanol series, starting with one-hour cycles of 70%, 96%, 96%, 100%, and 100% ethanol.
Place dehydrated samples through two 1 h cycles of xylene followed by two 1 h cycles of paraffin at 60 °C.
Paraffin-embed the samples in a mold and cool the samples down.
Cut the samples with a microtome in slices of 5 μm thick.
Rehydrate the samples by placing them in a returned graded ethanol series, starting with two washes of xylene for 5 min.
Wash the samples twice each in 100%, 95%, and 70% ethanol for 3 min per wash.
Finally, wash the samples three times in water for 2 min.
In case alginate is used to process samples, wash off the alginate with 10 mM citric acid prior to rehydration of paraffin sections.
Stain the samples with hematoxylin and eosin.
Stain the samples with Safranin-O.
Stain the samples with collagen I.
Stain the samples with collagen II.
Obtain papain digests of the scaffolds as described previously.
Perform an assay with a fluorescence-based DNA quantification kit to measure the double-strand DNA content of the scaffolds.
Express the amount of DNA per dry weight of the scaffold.
Perform a dimethylmethylene blue assay to quantify the remainder of the GAGs within the scaffold.
Express the amount in GAG per DNA.
Cut sterilized scaffolds from step 6.7 into 3 mm thick slices.
Transfer the scaffolds in separate wells of a 6-well plate.
Rehydrate scaffolds with cell culture medium by pipetting 1 mL of medium on top of the scaffold.
Let it soak for 30 min.
Prepare 3 x 10^6 cells in 100 μL of medium for each scaffold.
Pipette 50 μL of prepared cell suspension on top of the pre-soaked scaffold and incubate the scaffold for 1 h at 37 °C.
Carefully turn the scaffold upside down, pipet the remaining 50 μL of cell suspension on this side of the scaffold and incubate for 1 h at 37 °C.
After incubation, add 3 mL of medium to the wells.
Culture the cell-seeded scaffolds at 37 °C.
Handle the culture plate gently to avoid detachment of the cells.
Change the medium 2-3 times a week during culturing.
Cut the scaffolds in half after culturing for histology and biochemical analyses.
